chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Chur
spiritual_reading:
The assembly of those who are being instructed and prepared resembles a receptive state in the natural degree that can be made fruitful; into such a state the Divine, acting by means of one who ministers, introduces a living perception of good. That living perception takes up and reorders the entire strength and quality of the outward mind, and from the reordering it brings forth works that are genuinely good. When this perception has been made stable in the interiors, the inmost good that gives life is set in peace, and the Divine presence is at rest in the accomplished use.

In the same way, the living consciousness that is now involved in a confused conjunction with lower things longs to be raised into its own community of good and truth; yet it perceives and understands that, in itself, it has no passage opened anywhere within the totality of the lower and the higher faculties, because these, while disorder remains, act as constraint and distress and press upon it from every side. No opening is found except through the paired essentials that give spiritual discernment and natural discernment, from which illumination proceeds; in these it is given a place of quiet. Through them a passage is formed at the moment of emergence, and by means of that ordered illumination the consciousness is led out of mixture into the state where its own goods and truths are at home.

Yet even these illumining essentials find no settled repose among the whole range of intermediate faculties, except within the inmost state of pure enlightenment, which has been their own from eternity.

Thus the living consciousness is cleansed from every trouble that rose from disorder; and an interior quiet is provided for it, and an opening is made that grants entrance into the community where its own affections and perceptions belong.

And this inmost state of pure enlightenment becomes the final recipient for all illumination that proceeds into the higher and lower degrees; and there illumination is at rest and exercises dominion without end, because it is then conjoined to its origin and remains in order forever.

fills.notes: The assembly corresponds to a receptive natural state. Good earth is not merely ‘there’ but ‘prepared’ to receive influx, matching the spiritual sense: a receptacle that can be made fruitful before the planting of the living perception.

The tree ‘transforms the power and the quality of all earth’: power = strength/effectual force; quality = the determined state or disposition of the recipient plane. This matches the spiritual sense: reorders the entire strength and quality of the outward mind.

The powers of heaven and earth, while disorder persists, act as constraint and oppression ‘binding’ the soul on every side. This fits the correspondential notion of mixture producing restraint rather than a free passage.

The light-givers (sun and moon) correspond to the paired essentials of discernment from which illumination proceeds; the clause needs a connector expressing instrumental cause: the light-givers ‘whereby’ they become rest and a door.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by the correspondential structure already present in the natural text. The main restorations are ¶5 ‘made ready’ (receptive prepared ground), ¶5 ‘quality’ (state/disposition paired with power), ¶7 ‘binds’ (oppressive constraint of the mixed powers), and ¶7 ‘whereby’ (instrumental link from the light-givers to rest and exit). The remaining lacunae are trivial letter or obvious word completions.
